## Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 PCAP Analysis

**Evidence reviewed:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames). No IDS/Suricata alert files were present in the evidence directory — attribution below is derived entirely from packet content.

### Victim host

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** |
| MAC address | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** (domain `wiresharkworkshop.online`) |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** |

Confirmed via NBNS (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>`), Kerberos `CNameString` (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$`) exchanged with the domain controller 172.16.1.4 (`WIRESHARK-WS-DC`), and ARP mapping the IP to the MAC. Windows 11 Pro 64-bit confirmed by the malware's own beacon (below).

### Malware family

**STRRAT** (Java-based remote access trojan). **Attribution is signature-confirmed**, not behavioral — the C2 protocol is a cleartext, self-identifying string literally naming the malware:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

- Bot ID: `1BE8292C`
- Reported STRRAT version: `1.6`
- Reported AV: Windows Defender
- Beacon recurs every ~5 seconds for the remainder of the capture (TCP stream 83, port 172.16.1.66:49754 ↔ 141.98.10.79:12132, first seen at t=76.99s, running 508s to the end of the capture).
- No TLS handshake on this stream — plaintext raw TCP on a non-standard port, matching classic commodity-RAT C2 behavior.

### Indicators of Compromise (all grounded in capture)

**Command-and-control:**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — STRRAT C2, raw TCP, no supporting DNS lookup for this IP (hardcoded), confirmed via plaintext `ping|STRRAT|...` beacon strings.

**Suspicious supporting infrastructure (context, not independently confirmed malicious, but temporally tied to the infection):**
- DNS for `github.com` (→140.82.113.3) and `repo1.maven.org` (→199.232.196.209) resolved almost simultaneously at t≈63.96s, followed immediately by `objects.githubusercontent.com` (→185.199.110.133) at t≈64.77s.
- Two large TLS bursts followed within the next ~10 seconds: 833 KB from `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133) and 8.9 MB from `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209) — consistent with staged delivery of the STRRAT jar and/or a bundled JRE (STRRAT is Java-based) immediately before the C2 beacon starts at t=76.99s.
- `ip-api.com` (208.95.112.1) HTTP GET `/json/` at t=77.87s, right after the beacon starts — used to geolocate the host, matching the `US:United States` field in the STRRAT ping string.
- These three sessions are TLS-encrypted end to end. **No plaintext payload URL, downloaded filename, or file hash could be extracted from the capture** — do not treat these as confirmed malicious download URLs, only as the probable delivery vector by timing correlation.

**Malicious domains:** None observed in DNS — the confirmed C2 (141.98.10.79) was contacted by hardcoded IP with no corresponding domain lookup.

**Malicious URLs / transferred files / hashes:** None recoverable. No cleartext HTTP transfer of an executable/jar occurred; the only exported HTTP objects in the whole capture are benign (`www.msftconnecttest.com/connecttest.txt`, `ip-api.com/json/`). All suspicious transfers were TLS-encrypted, so no file name or SHA256 can be grounded in this evidence.

### Summary

Host DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as user `ccollier`, is infected with **STRRAT**. Around t=64s the host pulled data over TLS from GitHub and Maven Central infrastructure (contents unknown, encrypted), and roughly 13 seconds later began a persistent plaintext C2 beacon to **141.98.10.79:12132** that self-identifies as STRRAT and continues for the remainder of the capture. No file hashes or plaintext payload URLs are recoverable from this pcap alone.
